title: Aurora Systems - Procurement MSA/DPA & SLAs Review
summary: Redwood AE/SE reviewed MSA/DPA redlines, SLA targets, and onboarding steps. Customer raised concerns about data residency, encryption & KMS, and approval timing for pricing. Redwood agreed to share final MSA with tracked changes, security artifacts, and a pilot/pricing spreadsheet. Next steps include legal to exchange redlines, security to validate SOC2 docs, and procurement to approve PO and onboarding timeline.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-01
Start 17:00 UTC | Duration ~46 mins
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Evan Park (Redwood CSM), Carlos Vega (Aurora Head Security), Priya Kapoor (Aurora Procurement), Liam O'Connor (Aurora Legal), Sofia Ramos (Aurora Eng)

Summary (auto): Quick procurement/legal review of MSA/DPA, SLAs, and onboarding. Action items agreed.

00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan Blake from Redwood, i'm the AM on the account. we wanted to run through the MSA and DPA stuff, SLA questions, and timing for procurement.
00:14 Carlos: Hi Jordan, thanks, Carlos here. we got the initial docs, couple of redlines from our side but wanted to talk through the big ones — data residency, encryption at rest, and audit log retention.
00:28 Priya: Hi all, Priya from procurement. timeline is kinda tight; we need internal approvals by mid-december to get the vendor on boarded for our Q1 project. pricing needs to clear procurement + finance.
00:41 Liam: Liam (legal) — we'll focus on indemnities and liability caps, and need clarity on SLA credits and termination for convenience.
00:55 Maya: hi team, Maya Chen, i'm the SE. i'll cover what Redwood provides from a technical/security perspective — SOC2, ISO, SSO, KMS, VPC options, et cetera.
01:12 Jordan: Quick agenda: 1) MSA/DPA redlines 2) SLAs and operational support/credits 3) Pricing and procurement steps 4) Pilot/onboarding checklist. sound good?
01:22 Sofia: sounds good. also want to confirm private deployment options — we might need VPC peering or a dedicated tenant for certain PHI-ish flows.
01:33 Maya: yes, we support Redwood Private (private control plane) and Dedicated capacity. small note, sometimes in our docs that shows up as "Redwood Dedicated" or "Redwood Private" spelled differently, sorry for the mess in naming, but functionally we can provide VPC peering and on-prem connectors.
01:50 Carlos: on encryption, we need customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM). is that supported for logs and model artifacts?
02:02 Maya: short answer yes for most artifacts. we support Bring Your Own Key via KMS integrations and HSM for key wrapping. logs can be configured to redact PII and push to your SIEM. i'll share a short write-up after.
02:20 Carlos: okay, also DPA — our data residency is EU only for this workload. the DPA should insist on processing in eu-region only and not replicate outside.
02:32 Jordan: understood. we'll flag that as a DPA appendix, i think that's reasonable. one caveat is fallbacks for capacity; in rare cases we may route to nearest compatible region — we can make that explicit and require written approval.
02:48 Liam: liability cap: the MSA has a standard cap tied to fees; can we get language tying it to the prior 12 months of fees rather than the whole contract value?
03:02 Jordan: we can take that back — typical negotiation point. we'll send the MSA with Jordan's suggested redline.
03:10 Priya: procurement note — invoice terms; Aurora prefers Net45. does Redwood accept Net45?
03:20 Jordan: standard is Net30 but enterprise can accept Net45 with a PO. i'll mark that as a negotiation item.
03:30 Evan: from onboarding, we do a pilot for 30 days, success criteria usually latency and cost per 1k tokens, plus data handling sign-off. target timeline can be mid-december start.
03:45 Sofia: for the pilot we need model determinism and benchmarks; can we run a small benchmark against our prompt sets?
03:55 Maya: yes, we can run a bench — our SEs will run a 1k prompt test to measure latency and token cost, and we can capture KV cache and batch settings.
04:12 Carlos: also SOC2 — do you have the report and a point-in-time auditor letter? we'll need that for our security board.
04:24 Maya: yes, we have SOC2 Type II pdf and ISO27001 certs. i'll upload both plus a short guide on how our audit logs are structured. shared link: https://redwood-inference.com/security/soc2.pdf (note: we'll actually post to the secure share)
04:45 Liam: SLA specifics — the MSA draft lists 99.5% availability. for our production use we need 99.9% and an explicit SLO with credit schedule. also support response times and severity definitions.
04:59 Jordan: we typically offer 99.9% for enterprise Dedicated or Private with SLA credits tied to downtime minutes; Hosted tier is 99.5. we can adjust based on contract and reserved capacity.
05:15 Priya: what about financial remedies — do you do service credits only or can we negotiate penalty language?
05:25 Jordan: generally credits only, but terms can be discussed. legal and finance usually push back on monetary penalties.
05:33 Liam: ok let's see the credit schedule. also need a clause about data return/secure deletion at termination.
05:44 Maya: deletion is supported and we provide deletion receipts and audit log entries; for Private we can run the delete in-customer environment.
05:56 Carlos: DPA scope — does it include embeddings/derivatives? we want to ensure emergent models aren't used for training on our data.
06:10 Maya: by default our hosted models are not trained on customer data, and DPA can forbid training and model tuning using customer data. we'll add that clause. for Dedicated and Private variants, there's no cross-customer training.
06:26 Sofia: what's the backup policy? retention windows? we need to align with our retention schedules.
06:36 Maya: backups follow regional retention policies; default is 30 days for ephemeral caches, longer for logs depending on plan. we can capture that in the DPA appendix.
06:52 Priya: can you highlight the exact doc we'll need to route internally for approval? Security wants SOC2 and KMS integration docs, Legal wants MSA and DPA with tracked changes, Procurement needs pricing and PO terms.
07:08 Jordan: yes — we'll send: 1) MSA (tracked) v2 2) DPA template with residency appendix 3) Security artifacts bundle 4) pricing spreadsheet with seat/bundle options and pilot pricing 5) onboarding checklist and pilot SOW.
07:22 Carlos: timeline question again — if we get docs by Thursday, our legal can turn redlines in a week? that would align with your mid-Dec pilot start.
07:33 Liam: depends on internal calendar, but one week is realistic if there are no big changes.
07:40 Jordan: great — we'll aim to get docs by Thursday EOD.
07:46 (transcription glitch) Speaker 1: mm-hmm okay ok um
07:52 Maya: quick technical note about PKI — if you want client certs for VPC peering we can support mutual TLS for ingress to dedicated endpoints.
08:05 Sofia: good, that's preferred. we can do mTLS in front of private endpoints.
08:12 Priya: pricing — last spreadsheet showed tiered per-token plus reserved capacity. we need a clear number for procurement sign-off. also any onboarding credits?
08:26 Jordan: i'll include a final pricing tab with a recommended contract (12 months Reserved Dedicated) and a pilot pricing option with credits for the first month.
08:35 Priya: okay do we need legal signatures for the pilot?
08:40 Jordan: typically the pilot can run under a short form agreement or an interim SOW pending MSA finalization — legal usually wants at least the DPA and a short SOW.
08:50 Liam: short form SOW is fine but we want a clause that protects PII and prohibits training as discussed.
09:00 Maya: noted. i'll ensure the SOW includes the no-training clause and data handling specifics.
09:10 Carlos: auditing logs — can we get a sample schema? that will help our SIEM team.
09:18 Maya: yes sample logs with fields and redaction examples. i'll anonymize samples and upload.
09:25 Evan: on boarding timelines — once docs are signed we typically need two weeks to provision Dedicated capacity, shorter for hosted but longer for VPC peering.
09:38 Sofia: two weeks is acceptable. that fits our mid-Dec target if docs move fast.
09:45 (background talking)
09:52 Jordan: ok let's go through the MSA redlines we received: -- confidentiality duration asked for 5 years, your redline is 3. we can take to legal but probably meet in middle at 4?
10:08 Liam: 4 is acceptable if termination data deletion is explicit.
10:15 Jordan: we'll propose 4 years and explicit deletion cert.
10:20 Priya: procurement question: what's the approval chain — do you need a PO number to start provisioning?
10:27 Jordan: PO is required for invoicing and reserved capacity; pilot can start with a PO or short SOW plus billing terms.
10:36 Carlos: on DPA sub-processors — please enumerate typical cloud regions and sub-processors and their SOC2 details.
10:46 Maya: we'll send a sub-processor list with the SOC2 mappings; typically cloud infra partners are listed, and we include region mappings.
10:55 Liam: indemnity carveouts: can we clarify third-party IP claims? we want a clause that covers our use of outputs.
11:05 Jordan: we'll coordinate with legal, typical language shields customers for outputs produced by the model with disclaimers, but we can propose adding the specific carveout.
11:13 (15s pause)
11:29 Priya: timeline check — please confirm exact dates you'll send docs.
11:35 Jordan: Thursday EOD (2026-12-03) for docs, SE artifacts by Wednesday (2026-12-02), pilot kickoff tentatively 2026-12-15.
11:47 Carlos: ok, we'll aim to return redlines by 2026-12-08.
11:52 Liam: also need to see the SLA credit schedule and support hours — does Redwood offer 24/7 support for enterprise?
12:02 Jordan: 24/7 is available on enterprise support add-on, otherwise business hours with on-call for Sev1s. we'll include options in the pricing tab.
12:15 Sofia: one more technical — for on-prem connector, what's the network egress pattern? we need to know ports and mutal auth details.
12:26 Maya: we'll provide a network spec doc; default is HTTPS over 443 with mTLS option and outbound connections from your VPC to our ingress endpoints.
12:36 Priya: procurement needs a final list of approvers and any tax/VAT requirements for international invoicing. can Evan include a billing contact?
12:46 Evan: yes i'll include billing contact and sample invoice terms, plus VAT handling notes.
12:55 Jordan: ok let's do a quick recap of agreed items and owners.
13:02 Jordan: Redwood will send: MSA v2 (tracked) — Jordan; Security artifacts (SOC2/ISO, sub-processor list, KMS notes) — Maya; Pricing spreadsheet and SLA options — Jordan; Pilot SOW and onboarding checklist — Evan.
13:18 Carlos: Aurora will: Legal to return MSA/DPA redlines — Liam; Procurement to confirm PO and approvers — Priya; Security to validate SOC2 and KMS notes — Carlos.
13:30 Priya: point on procurement: we may need final number by 12/10 to meet finance cycle for December approvals.
13:39 Jordan: we'll aim to help hit that with docs on 12/03 and rapid follow-up.
13:45 (crosstalk)
13:52 Liam: small question on data purge — can you provide deletion certification language?
14:00 Maya: yes, we'll include deletion certificate language and process.
14:07 Jordan: all right, last thing: I'll upload the docs to the secure share and send calendar invite for the pilot kickoff.
14:16 Priya: thanks, appreciate it.
14:20 Carlos: thanks everyone.
14:24 Jordan: thanks all, we will follow up. end of call.

Post-call notes: Transcript has a few auto-caption glitches and one or two speaker attribution issues (Speaker 1 shows in middle). SE artifacts link to be shared securely, not public link.

Recap & Next steps (verbatim):
- Jordan to send MSA (tracked) and pricing spreadsheet by 2026-12-03
- Maya to upload SOC2/ISO/KMS docs by 2026-12-02
- Aurora to return legal redlines by 2026-12-08
- Pilot kickoff target 2026-12-15, provisioning ~2 weeks after signed PO
